subject: Onsite opt-in fallback & reconciliation — SF <> HubSpot mapping
messages:
From: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@brightwave.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onsite capture approach and fallback questions

Hi Jasmine / Laura,

Thanks again for the pre-show sync. A few follow-ups from our end as we finalize the floor ops runbook:

- Primary capture: badge scanner (USB tethered kiosk) that emits a CSV at end of day. See attached badge_scanner_spec.pdf for the exact schema.
- Fallback capture: web form QR for attendees who decline scanner or when kiosk is offline. We need the exact consent wording you want on the form for EU vs US attendees.
- Dupes: can you confirm Redwood's recommended dedupe key? Currently the badge CSV has badge_id, first_name, last_name, email, company, role, consent_flag.
- Salesforce vs HubSpot: what fields do you need mapped? We can include a sample export of daily CSV but want to avoid mapping drift mid-event.

Attachments: badge_scanner_spec.pdf, csv_field_map_v1.csv

Thanks,
Alex Ruiz
Ops Lead — BrightWave Events
alex.ruiz@brightwave.com
office +1 415-555-0189

From: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@brightwave.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:03:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onsite capture approach and fallback questions

Hi Alex — great notes, thanks. High level plan and asks below so we can lock the runbook: 

1) Dedupe key and canonical source
- Primary source: badge scanner CSV (end-of-day dump) will be treated as canonical for that day.
- Real-time ingestion: QR form entries will be ingested to HubSpot in near real-time; we will run a nightly reconciliation job to upsert to Salesforce.
- Dedupe: recommended key = email if present; fallback key = concat(lower(trim(first_name)),"|",lower(trim(last_name)),"|",company). Please flag if badge system can produce persistent badge_uid — that'd be ideal.

2) Consent wording
- For US attendees: use short opt-in line and a link to event privacy (we can host). Example: "I agree to receive follow-up communications from Redwood Inference and event partners. See privacy link."
- For EU attendees: must be explicit and separate opt-in checkbox (no pre-checked boxes). Example: "I consent to Redwood Inference processing my personal data for event follow-up. I understand I can withdraw consent at any time."
- Marissa — can you confirm exact phrase we should surface on the QR form? I added you to this thread.

3) Field mapping (SF <> HS)
- Please review attached csv_field_map_v1.csv and mark any missing fields. We want to map: first_name, last_name, email, company, role, opt_in_source, opt_in_timestamp, badge_id, event_id, referrer (qr/kiosk).
- Ben — we'll need a final mapping for HubSpot import properties and a Salesforce Lead import template so BrightWave can drop the daily file into the secure S3 drop.

Next steps: Alex to confirm badge_uid availability and expected daily CSV schedule. Marissa to confirm EU copy. Ben to share final import template.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Head of GTM Ops — Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@brightwave.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:22:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onsite capture approach and fallback questions

Quick notes from field ops standpoint: 

- Kiosk offline mode: badge scanner will queue scans locally and emit a full CSV every 4 hours if network flaps. We will also enable an end-of-day consolidated export. Nothing real-time guaranteed for offline mode.
- Duplicate badges: badge_uid is unique for checkin hardware model 4.2 — if Alex can confirm their units are 4.2+ we'll ingest badge_uid as persistent id. Otherwise we rely on dedupe key above.
- Suggested consent copy (place this under QR form and a small link near kiosk UI):
  "By submitting your details you agree to receive communications from Redwood Inference and event sponsors. For EU attendees, check the box to consent to personal data processing for event follow-up."

Attaching short list of approved phrases: consent_phrases.md

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Field Ops Manager

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onsite capture approach and fallback questions

Alex / team — attaching the final mapping CSV (hs_sf_mapping_final.csv) and a one-page ingestion checklist.

Notes: 
- HubSpot: set form to capture opt_in_source (kiosk/qr), utm if available, and a timestamp in ISO format. Make sure EU checkbox maps to a boolean HS property called EU_Consent.
- Salesforce: daily lead import should use externalId = badge_uid when present; otherwise we populate the composite dedupe key field so we don't create duplicates.
- Drop location: S3 (s3://redwood-events/brightwave/summit-2026/daily/) — BrightWave to push daily CSV by 11:00 PM PT. Our ingestion job runs at 01:00 AM PT and will reconcile against HubSpot exports.

Drive runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdEfGHjKL-mock-link

If that schedule works, we'll finalize the runbook and share signed manifest to ops.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Platform Ops — Redwood Inference
